add_channel.linkedin_desc: A browser window opens for you to log in to your LinkedIn profile. The login stays on this computer. Personal profiles first; company pages later.
add_channel.not_ready: Still being tested, not available yet
add_channel.social_desc: {hint}. The login stays on this computer and is used to post and collect data.
add_channel.wp_user_hint: Your WordPress login name; it needs permission to publish posts (Author or above)
add_channel.x_desc: The button below opens a browser window; sign in to X there. The login stays on this computer and is used for posting and data collection.
add_channel.xhs_desc: The button below opens a browser window; scan the QR code with the Xiaohongshu app. The login stays on this computer and is used for posting and data collection.

audit.desc: Checks titles, descriptions, H1, image alt, structured data, sitemap, llms.txt and page speed — things that affect search rankings and AI citations. The assistant can fix them; check the fixes on preview before going live.
audit.fix_all: Fix the issues from the audit of channel "{name}" (channel id {id}, site_ref {ref}), serious ones first. Push the fixes to preview, mark those issues as fixed-not-live, and tell me where to check (I'll publish with "Go live" on the Site check page).
audit.fix_all_btn: Hand all fixes to the assistant
audit.fix_all_wp: Fix the issues from the audit of WordPress channel "{name}" (channel id {id}, site {url}), serious ones first. Follow the WordPress part of the site-audit skill. Changes go live directly, so tell me each change first and make it only after I confirm, then re-run the audit.
audit.fix_one: Fix the audit issue "{title}" on {label} (site_issues id {id}, check {check}). Pages: {pages}
audit.fix_one_tail: . Push the fix to preview and mark this issue as fixed-not-live.
audit.fix_one_wp: . Follow the WordPress part of the site-audit skill. Changes go live directly, so tell me the change first and make it only after I confirm, then re-run the audit.
audit.fixing_desc: Check the preview first, then go live. After going live the site is checked again: fixed issues become resolved and move to Change reviews; the rest go back to to-fix.
audit.ignore_title: Not an issue; don't flag it in future checks
audit.label: channel "{name}" (site_ref {ref})
audit.never_desc: Crawls the site from your computer and scores it against a checklist. Takes 10–60 seconds, without the assistant or any model cost.
audit.no_site: No site channels yet. Add one under Sites & accounts to run a site check.
audit.passed_hint: No problems found in these checks; they cost no points
audit.plan_at_stale: Reviewed {when}; the site has been checked again since — consider reviewing again
audit.plan_req_hint: How the plan is structured, how detailed, which pages to focus on. Edit here and the next review follows it.
audit.r_index_checked: Status known for {n} of {total} indexable pages
audit.r_index_none: Link Google Search Console and each check will look up whether every page is indexed by Google, and why not.
audit.r_index_pending: The next check will look up every page's indexing status in Search Console.
audit.r_sitemap: Sitemap {path} in Search Console: {submitted} pages submitted, last read by Google {when}
audit.report_empty: This site hasn't been checked yet: click "Start check" first.
audit.review_hint: 17 days after going live, data before and after is compared — see Google rankings → Change reviews
audit.sg_ai: Make the site readable for AI search
audit.sg_ai_do: Allow AI search crawlers and add llms.txt and structured data so ChatGPT and Perplexity cite your site in answers.
audit.sg_broken_do: Dead pages and links through redirects waste Google's crawl and lose visitors. Point links at the final address, remove dead ones, and keep only working pages in the sitemap.
audit.sg_content: Make every page substantial and distinct
audit.sg_domain_do: Links and structured data still use other domains of this site (old system domain, preview, the www/non-www twin), splitting ranking signals across addresses. Use the main domain everywhere and redirect the others to it.
audit.sg_indexing_do: Pages Google hasn't indexed never show up in search, so nothing else matters until they are. Work through the reasons below: add substance to thin pages, link to unlinked ones, fix wrong canonicals and noindex tags, then request indexing in Search Console.
audit.sg_links_do: Google treats pages nothing links to as unimportant. Link them from the homepage, category pages and related articles, and add linked pages to the sitemap.
audit.title: Site check

channels.creght_failed: Couldn't read this site's creght data
channels.creght_needs_auth: The creght MCP isn't authorized yet. Authorize it in Settings → MCP to use this site's data and publishing.
channels.creght_not_in_account: This site isn't in the creght account you're connected to, so its data and publishing aren't available. Switch to the site's account in Settings → Connections (creght.cn and creght.com are separate regions).
channels.expired_hint: Sign-in expired: sign in again to keep publishing and collecting
channels.no_collect: Data collection for this channel isn't available yet.
channels.not_enabled_title: {platform} isn't set up in this project yet
channels.pending_desc: Add it to set up article publishing and inquiry sync here. A WordPress site needs its username and an application password once.
channels.pending_title: The website from setup, {host}, isn't added yet

ga4.desc: Link GA4 to see what built-in stats don't have: conversions (key events), traffic sources, sessions per page.
ga4.desc_wp: WordPress sites have no built-in traffic stats: link GA4 to see visits, sources and conversions here.
ga4.title: Google Analytics (GA4)

geo.answer_old: This is an older check that kept only the first 800 characters; re-run to see the full answer.
geo.ask_hint: Starts a new chat: the assistant looks into it with this answer, the pages it cited, other AIs’ answers and your data, and saves its conclusion here.
geo.ask_how: How do we get it to recommend us for this question?
geo.ask_ph: e.g. Where does this claim come from? What is wrong and what is true?
geo.ask_ph_rec: e.g. Why did it recommend these and not us? What content are we missing?
geo.ask_title: What do you want to ask? (about this {engine} answer)
geo.ask_why: Why doesn't it cite our site?
geo.checking_bg_hint: Started by the schedule or an earlier page; {n} done so far — each one shows up here as it finishes
geo.dedup: You already have {n} questions; duplicates were removed.
geo.desc: When buyers already know you and use ChatGPT to compare suppliers, is what the AI says right? When buyers don't know you yet, who does the AI recommend? Checks run from your computer, on your own network, with the models configured in Annulo, automatically once a week.
geo.eng_builtin: Works once signed in to creght, billed in AI credits
geo.eng_cli: Local agent, uses its own account and web search
geo.eng_cli_claude_hint: Searches with the local Claude Code, no credits used. It's Anthropic's model and search, so results show whether Claude recommends you, not ChatGPT. Each question takes a minute or two, and this computer has to be on.
geo.eng_cli_hint: Searches with the local Codex and the account it is signed in with, no credits used. Each question takes a minute or two, and this computer has to be on.
geo.eng_desc: Which provider and model configured in Annulo to ask ChatGPT with (it must support the OpenAI Responses API and web search). Providers and keys are managed in Annulo's Settings → Models — nothing to fill in here.
geo.eng_legacy: With no provider, the old local secret {key} is used
geo.eng_none: No engine is ready: open check settings and pick a provider
geo.eng_none2: No AI is turned on for checks
geo.eng_not_tested: Not tried yet: the first time, Chrome asks you to allow it
geo.eng_search_models: Models that can search the web:
geo.eng_search_only: Only models that can search the web; empty = {v}
geo.gen_title: Generated {n} questions — pick the ones to add
geo.hint_no_article: No article on your site answers this yet
geo.hint_no_rank: Your site doesn't rank on Google for these words yet
geo.kw_hint: Comma-separated. When this question cites you, these terms are more likely to bring you up in AI answers too.
geo.kw_ph: audiobook app, text to speech, TTS
geo.m_brand_legend: "New": you haven’t read this answer yet (opening the row marks it read). "Wrong": you marked it wrong. Green dot: the answer cites your site.
geo.m_col_off: {name} (turned off in check settings; showing the last results)
geo.m_no_cols: No AI is turned on for checks yet.
geo.m_rec_legend: ✓ cites your site   ◐ mentions you without a link   · neither   – not asked yet   ↑↓ more / fewer than this AI’s last check. Column headers show how many recommendation questions cited you in that AI’s latest check. Click a cell to read that answer and its sources.
geo.m_reported_n: {n} marked wrong, not looked into yet
geo.m_vis_title: Latest: recommendation questions citing you {c}/{n}, visibility {v}%
geo.mentioned_n: {n} more mentioned in the text without a link
geo.no_detail: This check left no details; it may have failed midway. Have the assistant run it again.
geo.no_searches: This answer didn't search the web.
geo.no_urls: The answer didn't cite any URLs.
geo.not_run_desc: Asks each question on every engine that has a provider picked in check settings (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Doubao), from your computer — a few seconds to over a minute each, without the assistant — and records the results.
geo.q_hint: Write it the way a buyer would type it into an AI, not as keywords.
geo.q_not_run: Not checked yet. Click Re-run check at the top right.
geo.q_ph: e.g. Which audiobook app has the most natural voices?
geo.report_hint: The assistant traces where that came from (your site isn't clear, another page is outdated, or your data isn't updated) and writes how to fix it
geo.report_ph: Write what the AI got wrong and what is actually true, e.g. we have 12 products, not 3; the MOQ is 300 pcs.
geo.req_hint: The assistant follows these every time it writes GEO questions. Change which kinds of questions, the language, or target markets here — the next batch follows the new version.
geo.rule: "Cited" means the answer links to a page on your site; "Mentioned" means your brand or domain appears in the text without a link — worth adding content for too.
geo.run_detail: Open to see each question's answer and citations in this check
geo.run_hint: Each question takes half a minute to over a minute; checked automatically every week
geo.run_hint2: The AIs you turned on are asked at the same time, half a minute to a minute or more per question; checks also run automatically once a week.
geo.s1_desc: Once buyers know your company name, products or website, they ask AI to research and compare. Here are ChatGPT's answers word for word, with the URLs they cite: you judge whether they're right (the data in the system may be out of date too); mark anything wrong and the assistant traces where it came from.
geo.s2_desc: Which sites the AI cites when buyers who don't know you yet ask questions, and whether it cites yours (visibility). Who gets cited depends largely on page quality and ranking, much like Google — compare with the Google ranking and your articles under each question.
geo.sites_title: Sites cited most in AI answers ({n} questions)
geo.step_no_query: (this AI does not show its search terms)
geo.sum_brand: {n} brand questions; {c} answers cited your site
geo.sum_lost: {n} questions no longer cite your site
geo.sum_rec: {n} recommendation questions; {c} cited your site; visibility {v}%
geo.vis_rule: Visibility = questions whose answer cites your site ÷ questions in this part (brand questions excluded)

publish.desc: An article can go to several sites. Each site needs a one-time publishing setup by the AI (reads the site's fields, writes the mapping, test-publishes); then just tick it.
publish.no_site: No sites yet. Add one so articles have somewhere to go.
publish.setup_desc: Not set up yet. The AI reads this site's article fields (and builds a blog if there isn't one), writes the mapping and test-publishes; then articles can be published here.
publish.title: Publish to sites

search.auto_title: Find the property matching the site's domain
search.b_links: Internal links (add links to this page from these pages)
search.b_links_ui: Internal links (these pages should link here)
search.cause_ctr_hint: Rank and impressions held but fewer people click: the title and description no longer appeal, or the results page now shows an AI overview or rich results from others. Rewrite the title and description first.
search.cause_demand_hint: Fewer people search: it may be seasonal (check whether the bars dip at this time every year), or some queries were lost. If it is not seasonal, refresh the content around the lost queries; if it is, click "Ignore".
search.cause_rank_hint: Average rank is 2+ places worse than at the peak: the content is likely outdated, or others cover it better. Have AI outline a refresh based on the queries that lost the most.
search.choose_range: Choose a start and end date, then apply them.
search.decay_desc: Pages that used to bring clicks from Google but got clearly fewer in the last 28 days: compared with their best of the previous five 28-day periods, clicks fell by over 30% (searches for your company name excluded). Checked automatically every week.
search.decay_lost_hint: Total, each against its own peak 28 days
search.decay_never: Not checked yet. Click "Check again" to read the last six 28-day periods; after that it runs every week.
search.decay_no_record: No impressions in the last 28 days; sync Google rankings first
search.decay_none: No page has clearly declining traffic. It is checked again every week.
search.decay_pages_hint: Clicks down over 30% from their peak
search.decay_period: Peak: {start} – {end}; bars are clicks over the last six 28-day periods
search.empty: No data synced yet, or the site had no Google impressions in the last 28 days. Click Sync now; new sites usually take a few weeks to get impressions.
search.empty_range: No Google Search data for the selected dates. New sites usually take a few weeks to get impressions.
search.ga4_desc: Website traffic, users, sources and conversions from Google Analytics (GA4).
search.gaps_desc: People search these on Google, but no page on your site ranks (average position beyond 15). Each sync adds them to the topics; write articles to capture these searches.
search.invalid_range: Choose valid dates: start must be on or before end, and end must be no later than {latest}.
search.link_desc: Connect a Google account in Annulo once (read-only) to see clicks, impressions and positions for every page here. Data syncs daily.
search.link_offline: Open the back office from Annulo to connect.
search.meta_req_hint: The assistant follows these every time it rewrites a page title and description. Change the style, must-have words or where the brand goes here — the next rewrite follows the new version.
search.no_prev: No data for the previous period
search.no_props_1: This Google account has no Search Console properties yet. Go to
search.no_props_2: to add and verify your site, then come back and refresh.
search.no_queries: No query data for this day (Google omits low-volume queries).
search.noise: {n} impressions from brand terms and site: queries excluded
search.opp_low_ctr_hint: Plenty of impressions, but CTR is under half of what this position usually gets: the title and description aren't earning the click
search.opp_striking_hint: Average position 8–20: a bit more content could get it onto page one
search.pick_day: Click a day on the chart to see its top queries and pages.
search.refresh_prompt:
Refresh the page {page} on channel "{name}" ({site}) following the outline below (search_pages id {id}). The page used to get {peak} clicks from Google in 28 days and got only {now} in the last 28 days: update what is outdated and cover what people searching these terms want to know.

{brief}

How: pull the channel site to $HOME/.shuttle/sites/{site_id} the way the site-audit / websites skill does (creght pull if already pulled), then edit this page per the outline: update outdated information, add sections and FAQ, and add links to it from the pages in the internal links list. Do not change the page URL and do not invent facts that are not on the page or in the project profile (ask me first, or leave a marked placeholder, where the outline says I need to provide something).
When done, creght push to the preview, set this search_pages record status to fixing, and tell me where to look in the preview. Do not publish: once I confirm and it is live, I will click "Live, start review" myself.
search.synced_28_days: Suggestions use the latest 28 days from the daily sync.
search.unlink_hint: Automatic sync pauses for this site and historical data is kept. Linking again resumes sync.
search.unlinked: Unlinked. Automatic sync is paused. Link a site below to resume.
search.wordpress_ga4: View WordPress website traffic under GA4 traffic.
search.worth_desc: Sorted by impressions, excluding brand terms and site: queries (not real search demand). Expected CTR is a rule of thumb by position, used only to spot clearly low pages.

site.no_visits: No visits in this period. Only published sites are counted; previews aren't.
site.offline: Traffic data is read by Annulo on your computer. Run annulo in a terminal and open the back office from the localhost address it prints.
site.referrer_empty: No external referrers yet; direct visits aren't counted

site_visits.desc: Visits, sources, pages and regions of your Creght site.
site_visits.no_site: No site yet. Add your site in Sites & accounts to see its traffic here.
